      Vikram University was established in Ujjain on 1 March 1957. Shri Ranchod Lalji Dhabai donated the land for it from Barnagar. The foundation stone of Vikram University was laid by the then Home Minister of India Shri Govind Vallabh Pant on 23 October 1956. The function was presided over by the Rajpramukh of Madhya Bharat State Late Jiwajirao Scindia.
      971-
      972:The state of Madhya Pradesh was formed in 1956, and Madhya Bharat was merged into it. The Act relating to the University was accordingly amended. The amended Act of Vikram University No. 13, 1957 was published in Madhya Pradesh Gazette on 16 August 1957.
      973-
      974:The University's jurisdiction diminished due to the 1964-65 formation of Indore University, Gwalior and Bhopal University during 1969-70. On 20 April 1973, the Governor granted permission to bring about homogeneity in the organization and administration of Madhya Pradesh Universities. This permission was first published in the Madhya Pradesh Gazette (extraordinary) on 23 April 1973. By a notification of the Education Department 940/20/8/71 dated 3 May 1973, the by-laws of the Madhya Pradesh Universities Act No. 1 to 19 were brought into effect from 25 September 1973, No. 20 to 26 from 1 December 1973, and No. 27 to 31 from 4 May 1974, for all the Universities of Madhya Pradesh (including Vikram University).
      975-
      976:The Madhya Pradesh Universities Act was amended and published in Madhya Pradesh Gazette on 28 June 1985. As per the amendment, University Jurisdiction was redefined and demarcated in accordance with the Revenue districts of Ujjain Division, including Ujjain, Ratlam, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Shajapur and Dewas. Because of the new jurisdiction, the number of affiliated colleges decreased, and some new colleges were granted affiliation.

Chatterjee... Read Full History The department saw eminent geologists like Prof. Singh, Prof. Lahiri, Prof. Verma, and many more shaping it through the decades. Key developments include UGC support, expansion into applied geology, and robust infrastructure for M.Sc. and Ph.D. studies. Prof. S. C. Chatterjee took the charge of the Department on the 15th July, 1960, and immediately the developmental work had begun in a portion of the Vigyan Bhavan building allocated for this Department. It remained there till November, 1964, when it was shifted to Ujjain. As the Departmental building has been under construction, it was housed in the Library Building for about two years and could move finally to its own on the 5th of December, 1966. The department was fortunate to have Late Prof. Satya Charan Chatterjee, D. Sc., P. R. S., F. G. S., F. N. A. as its founder Professor & Head in 1961 (formerly J. N. Tata Professor of Geology, Patna University). With his extraordinary brilliance and visionary power, Prof. Chatterjee lifted this department to international level, particularly in the aspects of Petrologic studies. Prof. Chatterjee developed a dedicated team of sincere teachers and researchers which included Late Prof. D. K. Chakravarty (a geology teacher of national repute from Banaras Hindu University), Prof. Surendra K. Saxena, Late Prof. Gyananand Saxena (famous palaeontologist who later shifted to Sagar), Late Dr. S. Subba Rao (famous volcanic petrologist) and Prof. Ashok Lahiri (Professor at B. M. Birla Science & Technology Centre, Jaipur). Several eminent scholars served this department as faculty member for a short span of time during 1960-1963 includingDr. M. S. Rao, Dr. S. C. Mohan, Dr. Mahendra Singh, Dr. Harfan Ali, Dr. Ramesh. K. Shrivastava and Dr. Noman Ghani. The department shifted to Ujjain in 1964, temporarily in the Maharaja Jiwaji Rao Library Building, and finally to the present house in December, 1966. After his superannuation from regular assignments of Vikram University in 1970, Prof. Chatterjee was elevated as Emeritus Professor of Geology. Late Prof. S. C. Chatterjee had a list of achievements and contributions - just to name a few of them - member, International Petrologic Commission; Section President, Geology and Geography Section, Indian Science Congress; Chairman, UGC Standing Committee on Geology etc. Prof. Krishna Kant Singh took over as Head of this department in December 1971. Prof. Singh earned his basic degree in Geology from BHU, Varanasi and served in different capacity at IIT, Kharagpur, University of Sagar and University of Roorkee. He left this department in 1990 to take over as Vice-Chancellor of Jiwaji University, Gwalior. Prof. Singh gave a new dimension to the department by introducing the concept of Applied Geology. Prof. Singh, with his sincere efforts and approval of UGC, started one year course of Master of Science in Technology (Applied Geology) in Mineral Exploration. The course earned high reputation and, different national and international companies recruited these students through campus interview or by direct call letter. Prof. Singh was a UGC National Professor, a specialist in Ore Geology, a beloved teacher, a successful administrator and a perfect gentleman who took this department to the world of modern technology. They get knowledge of different branches of Microbiology and Food Technology like, Food Microbiology, Industrial Microbiology, Environmental Microbiology, Microbial Genetics, Medical Microbiology, Food Processing, Food Packaging, Food Preservation etc. Moreover, students undertake dissertation, surveys, industrial/ laboratory visits as part of curricula and hence, get exposure to practical aspects of the subject. Student take part in group discussions, seminars etc. and broaden their knowledge base which help them to find suitable placement in different Government and private organizations. Vision: To be a leading center of excellence in microbiology and food technology, fostering innovation, research, and sustainable solutions to enhance food safety, quality, and human health. Mission: To provide high-quality education and training in microbiology and food technology, equipping students with scientific knowledge and practical skills. To conduct innovative research that addresses global challenges in food safety, biotechnology, and microbial sciences. To collaborate with industries, government agencies, and research institutions for the advancement of food technology and microbiology. To promote sustainable practices and the development of safe, nutritious, and high-quality food products. Chatterjee took the charge of the Department on the 15th July, 1960, and immediately the developmental work had begun in a portion of the Vigyan Bhavan building allocated for this Department. It remained there till November, 1964, when it was shifted to Ujjain. As the Departmental building has been under construction, it was housed in the Library Building for about two years and could move finally to its own on the 5th of December, 1966. The department was fortunate to have Late Prof. Satya Charan Chatterjee, D. Sc., P. R. S., F. G. S., F. N. A. as its founder Professor & Head in 1961 (formerly J. N. Tata Professor of Geology, Patna University). With his extraordinary brilliance and visionary power, Prof. Chatterjee lifted this department to international level, particularly in the aspects of Petrologic studies. Prof. Chatterjee developed a dedicated team of sincere teachers and researchers which included Late Prof. D. K. Chakravarty (a geology teacher of national repute from Banaras Hindu University), Prof. Surendra K. Saxena, Late Prof. Gyananand Saxena (famous palaeontologist who later shifted to Sagar), Late Dr. S. Subba Rao (famous volcanic petrologist) and Prof. Ashok Lahiri (Professor at B. M. Birla Science & Technology Centre, Jaipur). Several eminent scholars served this department as faculty member for a short span of time during 1960-1963 includingDr. M. S. Rao, Dr. S. C. The department shifted to Ujjain in 1964, temporarily in the Maharaja Jiwaji Rao Library Building, and finally to the present house in December, 1966.
